title: Derived left extension from coefficient levels
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ an inverse sequence of sheaves of commutative rings. Let $\mathscr S(B)$ be the category of strict semilinear systems: an object consists of $B_n$-module sheaves $M_n$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $B_{n+1}$-linear maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{B_{n+1}\to B_n}M_n$; morphisms commute with these maps. Restriction of scalars has the meaning of [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Use its unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $\mathscr S(B)$ is Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Its coproducts and cohomology, and the coproducts of its unbounded derived category, are evaluated componentwise. The exact evaluations $e_n:D(\mathscr S(B))\to D(B_n)$ jointly detect isomorphisms and cohomological bounds.

For each $n\ge1$, $e_n$ has a left adjoint $L_n$, with natural evaluation formulas
$$e_mL_nP=\begin{cases}B_m\otimes^L_{B_n}P&m\le n,\\0&m>n.\end{cases}$$
Here derived change of ring has the meaning of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. More generally, let $r:\mathbf Z_{\ge1}\to\mathbf Z_{\ge1}$ be strictly increasing and unbounded, let $B_r=(B_{r(i)})_{i\ge1}$, and let $U_r:D(\mathscr S(B))\to D(\mathscr S(B_r))$ be exact restriction of systems. It has a left adjoint $L_r$. Put $t(m)=\min\{i:r(i)\ge m\}$. There is a natural formula
$$e_mL_rN=B_m\otimes^L_{B_{r(t(m))}}N_{t(m)}.$$
More precisely, put $a=t(m)$ and $b=t(m+1)$. The adjoint transition from $m+1$ to $m$ is
$$B_m\otimes^L_{B_{m+1}}e_{m+1}L_rN\cong B_m\otimes^L_{B_{r(b)}}N_b\longrightarrow B_m\otimes^L_{B_{r(a)}}N_a=e_mL_rN,$$
where the arrow is induced by the adjoint structure map $B_{r(a)}\otimes^L_{B_{r(b)}}N_b\to N_a$ of $N$. For $a=b$ this structure map is the identity; for $a<b$ it is the specified selected-level transition. All identifications use the canonical derived tensor associators. These are functors and adjunctions on the derived category of strict systems, with actual natural units and counits, not just formulas for unrelated evaluated objects. They are the total left derived functors of the strict-system left extensions along the singleton and subsequence inclusions, respectively, with the displayed evaluations. Their left-extension universal properties are the ordinary derived-category adjunctions just stated. Their adjunction identifications are compatible with composition of subsequence restrictions and the canonical tensor associators. No flatness of $B_{n+1}\to B_n$, normalization, or boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: Realize systems as modules on one small ringed site. Let $J$ be the ordered category of positive integers with one arrow $m\to n$ for $m\le n$, and give $\mathcal C\times J$ the coverings $\{(U_i,n)\to(U,n)\}$ coming from coverings of $U$ in $\mathcal C$. Pulling such a covering back along $(V,m)\to(U,n)$ gives $\{(V\times_U U_i,m)\to(V,m)\}$, so the site axioms hold. Define $\mathcal B(U,n)=B_n(U)$, with restriction along $(V,m)\to(U,n)$ induced by $B_n\to B_m$ and restriction to $V$. The sheaf condition is exactly the sheaf condition at each level. Consequently a $\mathcal B$-module sheaf is exactly a strict semilinear system, and a complex of such sheaves is a strict complex of systems, including its maps. Apply [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] to this small site and sheaf of commutative rings. This proves that $\mathscr S(B)$ is Grothendieck abelian. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], kernels are sectionwise, cokernels and colimits are sheafified sectionwise constructions. Since coverings never change the level, these constructions are the corresponding module-sheaf constructions at each level. Thus exactness, coproducts, and cohomology of complexes are componentwise.

source.place: Tags 03DA (lemma-abelian), 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A5 (section-unbounded). The product-site construction is written out here, generalizing Zheng Construction 4.1.

proof.text: Small coproducts of short exact sequences in $\mathscr S(B)$ are exact: each coproduct is the filtered colimit, over finite subsets of its indexing set, of finite direct sums, and filtered colimits are exact by the Grothendieck property established in step 1. Hence termwise coproducts preserve quasi-isomorphisms. They also give coproducts in the unbounded derived category. Indeed for any family of complexes $K_i$ and target $M$, choose a K-injective resolution $M\to I$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on the product ringed site. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], morphisms from any complex to $I$ in the derived category are chain maps modulo homotopy. A chain map $\bigoplus_i K_i\to I$ is exactly a family of chain maps $K_i\to I$, and a homotopy is exactly a family of homotopies. Therefore $\operatorname{Hom}_{D}(\bigoplus_i K_i,M)=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_{D}(K_i,M)$, with the coprojections induced by those of complexes. This proof applies to every small indexing set, including the empty set; it does not apply a countable-sum lemma to an arbitrary family. Evaluation thus preserves these derived coproducts. Evaluations descend to exact triangulated functors by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. For a morphism $h$, every $e_n h$ is an isomorphism if and only if every $e_n\operatorname{Cone}(h)$ is acyclic, if and only if $\operatorname{Cone}(h)$ is acyclic. Likewise $H^q(M)=0$ if and only if $H^q(e_nM)=0$ for every $n$. This proves joint detection of isomorphisms and of either cohomological bound, with one common bound for all levels.

source.place: Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective); injectives.tex Tag 079P; derived.tex Tag 015F. The coproduct universal-property argument is written out for arbitrary small families.

proof.text: Construct the underived evaluation adjunction. For a $B_n$-module sheaf $P$ put $(E_nP)_m=B_m\otimes_{B_n}P$ for $m\le n$, and zero for $m>n$. Below $n$ use the coefficient-map-induced tensor transitions; the transition out of the zero region is zero. On a map use $1\otimes h$. Ordinary tensor/restriction adjunction is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], applied to the identity topos and each map $B_n\to B_m$. A map $h:P\to M_n$ determines at $m\le n$ the tensor-adjoint of $P\xrightarrow{h}M_n\to\operatorname{Res}_{n,m}M_m$; above $n$ use zero. These components commute with transitions because the transitions of $M$ compose. Conversely a system map $E_nP\to M$ has these components by naturality from level $n$. Evaluation there is its inverse, so this gives a bijection natural in $P,M$, hence $E_n\dashv e_n$. The unit is $P\cong B_n\otimes_{B_n}P$, and the counit has at level $m\le n$ the adjoint of the transition $M_n\to\operatorname{Res}_{n,m}M_m$, and zero above $n$. The same formulas degree by degree give the termwise adjunction on complexes.

proof.text: Construct the underived subsequence adjunction. Unboundedness of $r$ makes $t(m)$ exist, and strict increase gives $t(r(i))=i$ and $t(m)\le t(m+1)$. For a strict $B_r$-system $N$ set $(E_rN)_m=B_m\otimes_{B_{r(a)}}N_a$, $a=t(m)$. When $b=t(m+1)$, take the transition adjunct to be $B_m\otimes_{B_{r(b)}}N_b\to B_m\otimes_{B_{r(a)}}N_a$, obtained by tensoring the transition of $N$ and using the ordinary tensor associator; when $a=b$ use the identity transition of $N_a$. More generally use the same prescription for $m'\ge m$. It composes because $N$'s transitions compose and both ways of multiplying three scalar factors give the same balanced tensor map. For a map $h:N\to U_rM$, define $E_rN\to M$ at $m$ as the scalar adjunct of $N_a\xrightarrow{h_a}M_{r(a)}\to\operatorname{Res}_{r(a),m}M_m$. Write $\tau^N_{j,i}$ and $\tau^M_{v,u}$ for the iterated semilinear transitions. For $m'\ge m$, put $a'=t(m')$ and $a=t(m)$. On a local pure tensor $c\otimes x$, $x\in N_{a'}$, both paths in the system-map square give $c\,\tau^M_{r(a'),m}h_{a'}(x)$: the path through level $m$ gives $c\,\tau^M_{r(a),m}h_a\tau^N_{a',a}(x)$, which is the same by $h_a\tau^N_{a',a}=\tau^M_{r(a'),r(a)}h_{a'}$ and composition of $M$'s transitions. Pure tensors generate the tensor presheaf and then its sheafification, so this proves the square on module sheaves. Conversely evaluate a system map at $m=r(i)$, where $(E_rN)_{r(i)}=N_i$; its components at other $m$ are forced by the arrow from $r(t(m))$ to $m$. These constructions are inverse and natural, so $E_r\dashv U_r$. The unit is the identity under $U_rE_rN=N$. The counit has components $B_m\otimes_{B_{r(t(m))}}M_{r(t(m))}\to M_m$ induced by the actual transitions. Evaluating this counit at selected levels is the identity; applying it to $E_rN$ is the identity because $t(r(t(m)))=t(m)$. These verify the two triangle identities. The construction is additive and gives the termwise adjunction on complexes.

proof.text: Obtain simultaneous K-flat representatives on the tower site of step 1. Evaluation on sheaves of sets preserves finite limits, computed componentwise. Its right adjoint sends a sheaf $A$ to the tower with value $A$ at $m\ge n$, terminal sheaf at $m<n$, identity transitions within each region, and the unique boundary transition: a map into this tower is uniquely its component $M_n\to A$. Thus evaluation is the inverse image of a morphism of topoi. It sends the tower ring $\mathcal B$ to $B_n$, with identity structural ring map, so its module pullback is exactly $e_n$. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the small ringed tower site to get $Q\to N$ K-flat with flat terms and termwise surjective. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] applied to each evaluation morphism, every $Q_n$ is K-flat over $B_n$ with flat terms. Since evaluation is exact, every $Q_n\to N_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The same construction applies to $B_r$. In particular every complex of systems has one strict representative with all these properties simultaneously; independently chosen level resolutions are not being assembled.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution) and 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat); the evaluation geometric morphism is explicitly Construction 4.1 of Zheng, printed p. 21.

proof.text: For $E_n$ take the resolving class of flat-term K-flat $B_n$-complexes; it resolves every complex by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. For $E_r$ take the class of strict system complexes whose every component is flat-term K-flat; step 5 proves it resolves every complex. Both functors are additive. Hence they preserve homotopies, shifts and cones termwise: a cone has terms $Y^k\oplus X^{k+1}$ and a matrix differential, and additivity preserves this direct sum and each matrix entry. Using [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated], their composites from the homotopy categories to the target derived categories are exact. If $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism between objects of the relevant resolving class, every component of $E_ns$ or $E_rs$ is a change of rings of a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes (or $0\to0$). It is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](1). Componentwise cohomology from step 1 makes this a quasi-isomorphism of systems. Therefore [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] gives everywhere-defined exact functors $L_n=\mathbf L E_n$ and $L_r=\mathbf L E_r$, with natural comparisons to $E_n$ and $E_r$ which are invertible on these resolving classes.

source.place: Tags 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes), dual part, and 05SE (proposition-derived-functor), LF exactness; sites-cohomology.tex 06YS and 06YT.

proof.text: The exact functors $e_n$ and $U_r$ induce the termwise functors on derived categories by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. These are also their everywhere-defined right derived functors by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. In the ind-system convention of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors], for a complex $K$ every quasi-isomorphism $K\to K'$ is carried by $e_n$ or $U_r$ to a quasi-isomorphism, so every transition of the filtered system $(F(K'))_{K\to K'}$ is an isomorphism in the target derived category. That system is therefore essentially constant with value $F(K)$, the identity stage giving the representing cocone; this is the right-hand existence hypothesis at every complex. To check the existence convention for deriving adjoints explicitly, quasi-isomorphisms in either source homotopy category have a right calculus of fractions and two-out-of-three by [lem-pur-quasi-isos-saturated-triangulated]. The resolving classes and invariance verified in step 6 therefore satisfy [lem-pur-resolving-class-essential-constancy]: the left-derived denominator pro-systems are essentially constant at every complex, with invertible identity leg on the resolving classes. By [lem-pur-left-derived-defined-pointwise-kan-bridge], these values and comparisons identify with the left derived functors of step 6, including their specified comparison on representatives. All hypotheses of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] now hold for each underived adjunction of steps 3 and 4. Consequently $L_n\dashv e_n$ and $L_r\dashv U_r$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. This produces natural units and counits satisfying the triangle identities; it never assumes that evaluation preserves K-injectives.

Fix the normalization of these adjunctions on representatives. By [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] the termwise adjunctions of steps 3 and 4 induce the Hom bijections on homotopy categories. Apply the explicit formula of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] with the exact right functor, its identity-stage right-derived comparison, and the left-derived comparisons of step 7. For $P$ in the relevant resolving class and a chain map $g:P\to R K$ ($E\dashv R$ means either pair), take the two denominators to be identities. The formula says that the transpose of the class of $g$ is the class of its strict transpose $EP\to K$, composed with $LE(QP)\cong Q(EP)$. In particular the derived unit at $QP$ is represented by the strict unit $P\to REP$. For a resolution $p:P\to RK$, the derived counit at $QK$ is represented by the strict transpose $EP\to K$, after identifying $LE(RQK)\cong Q(EP)$ using $p$. Naturality extends these descriptions to all objects and morphisms. Thus the adjunctions have the specific tensor-adjoint units and counits, rather than merely some adjunction between the same functors.

source.place: Tags 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general) and 09T5; use identity denominators and then a resolving denominator in the explicit formula.

proof.text: For $P\in D(B_n)$ take a flat-term K-flat resolution $Q\to P$. Step 6 represents $L_nP$ by $E_nQ$, so [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](2) gives $e_mL_nP=B_m\otimes^L_{B_n}P$ below $n$ and zero above. For a system $N$ take the single strict resolution $Q\to N$ of step 5 for $B_r$. Then $L_rN$ is represented by $E_rQ$ and $Q_a$ is flat-term K-flat for every $a$. Hence $e_mL_rN=B_m\otimes^L_{B_{r(t(m))}}N_{t(m)}$, naturally in $N$. These are evaluations of one derived functor with the comparison of step 6. On maps of representatives the component is $1\otimes h_{t(m)}$; the natural comparison and localization define the action on arbitrary derived morphisms. Moreover each component of $E_rQ$ is itself flat-term K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], for the identity topos and the indicated ring map. Thus it is again an admissible representative for subsequent left extensions.

proof.text:
Write $a=t(m)$ and $b=t(m+1)$. On the same $Q$ the strict transition of $E_rQ$ is precisely the tensor-adjoint of the selected transition $Q_b\to\operatorname{Res}_{B_{r(b)}\to B_{r(a)}}Q_a$ used in step 4. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], both $Q_b$ and $B_{m+1}\otimes_{B_{r(b)}}Q_b$ are flat-term K-flat over their respective rings. Consequently the ordinary chain isomorphism
$$B_m\otimes_{B_{m+1}}(B_{m+1}\otimes_{B_{r(b)}}Q_b)\cong B_m\otimes_{B_{r(b)}}Q_b$$
computes the derived associator. Explicitly $(c\otimes d)\otimes x$ maps to $c\overline d\otimes x$, with inverse inserting $1$ in the intermediate ring; these balanced formulas sheafify by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. By the normalized scalar transposition of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], the chain map induced from $Q_b\to\operatorname{Res}Q_a$ represents exactly the specified derived adjoint structure map of $N$. Its further scalar extension is therefore the arrow in the statement, including its source, target and canonical associators. If $a=b$ it uses the identity of $Q_a$; if $a<b$ it uses the actual iterated transition. This proves the transition formula, rather than testing equality of arbitrary system morphisms by evaluations.

proof.text: The left-extension terminology has its ordinary derived meaning here. For a singleton inclusion or the selected-index inclusion $r$, the strict left extension is the functor $E_n$ or $E_r$ of steps 3 and 4: its maps to a strict system are exactly the maps after restriction. Step 6 derives that functor, and step 7 gives its left-extension universal property on the ordinary derived categories. The unit description of step 8 fixes the restriction-to-extension map in that property. At $m$ the singleton comma category is empty for $m>n$ and has its sole object for $m\le n$. For $r$ its objects are $i$ with $r(i)\ge m$, with arrows from larger to smaller indices; its terminal object is $t(m)$. This accounts for the single tensor term in the formulas. None of this identifies $D(\mathscr S(B))$ with a category of diagrams in the ordinary categories $D(B_n)$, nor requires an enhanced section equivalence.

proof.text:
Let $s$ be a strictly increasing unbounded selection of $B_r$, put $a=t_r(m)$ and $c=t_s(a)$. Then $r(s(i))\ge m$ if and only if $s(i)\ge a$, if and only if $i\ge c$, so $t_{r\circ s}(m)=c$. Choose a strict componentwise flat-term K-flat resolution $Q\to N$ over $B_{r\circ s}$. Step 9 shows that $E_sQ$ is componentwise flat-term K-flat, so step 6 computes $L_rL_sN$ by $E_rE_sQ$. The strict tensor associator identifies its $m$th component
$$B_m\otimes_{B_{r(a)}}(B_{r(a)}\otimes_{B_{r(s(c))}}Q_c)\cong B_m\otimes_{B_{r(s(c))}}Q_c.$$
This gives a map of strict system complexes to $E_{r\circ s}Q$: each transition uses the same iterated transition of $Q$, and the associator multiplies the same scalar factors on either path. Its inverse inserts $1$; both formulas are balanced and sheafify by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], these chain associators compute the corresponding derived tensor associators. Thus the simultaneous representatives compute the proposed composite comparison.

source.place: Tag 0G7E; explicit ordinary tensor associators on simultaneous K-flat representatives, extending Zheng Construction 4.1.

proof.text: Define the composite comparison on all derived morphisms by adjunction. Both $L_rL_s$ and $L_{r\circ s}$ are left adjoint to $U_sU_r=U_{r\circ s}$. Define the comparison to be the unique map whose transpose is the unit of $L_{r\circ s}$ under the composite Hom adjunction, and its inverse by the reverse prescription. The two composites transpose to the respective units, so are identities. The bijections are natural, so this is a natural isomorphism preserving the adjunction identifications, units and counits. On the simultaneous representatives of step 12, the normalized transposes of step 8 show that this is exactly the tensor associator there: restriction to selected indices is the identity and all other components are forced by the strict transitions. The composite-unit and composite-counit formulas and compatibility of transposition with composition are [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2). For three selections the two comparison paths transpose to the same triple composite unit by that formula, so they agree; the identity selection gives the identity unit and identity comparison. This proves composition compatibility in the ordinary derived categories. Exactness and shift compatibility already follow from step 6; no model-category suspension computation is needed. No flatness of coefficient maps, normalization, or boundedness was introduced.
